title: Requirements, Design, Implementation, and Review Cycle
learningObjectives: Describe how requirements guide design and implementation.
Explain why review and feedback are part of development.
Identify how tests relate to requirements.
Recognize iterative development rather than a rigid one-way process.
Trace a small change from requirement through verification and review.

understand.concept: A development cycle connects a need to an implemented and verified change. A team clarifies requirements and constraints, chooses a design, implements code, tests it, reviews the change, and learns from feedback. These activities are iterative: review or testing may reveal an unclear requirement or design that needs adjustment. Traceability helps confirm that a change addresses the intended need and that important behavior is checked. The cycle is a useful guide, not a rigid sequence that forbids revisiting earlier steps.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear design boundaries and intentional development practices help teams maintain software, verify changes, and respond to real needs.
understand.analogy: Think of a team coordinating a shared task: clear responsibilities and feedback loops help everyone work toward the same result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software design includes precise technical constraints and interactions that teamwork analogies cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative: Start with a clear statement of what should happen and how success will be observed. Design a manageable approach, implement it, and create tests that cover the requirement and important edge cases. Review the code for correctness, clarity, and safety. Incorporate feedback and update documentation when behavior or interfaces change. Keep the change focused so reviewers can understand it.

commonMistakes: Treating design smells as automatic defects.
Overengineering small projects with unnecessary layers or patterns.
Mixing requirements, features, and refactoring without clear intent.
Ignoring tests or edge cases when changing structure.
Failing to consider project context and trade-offs.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Choose a small feature request and write its success criteria. Sketch the design and identify one risk. Implement a simple version. Create tests for normal and boundary behavior. Review the change against the original requirement and note any feedback.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Plan and implement a small feature in a sample project. Write a short requirement with measurable acceptance criteria. Describe your design decision. Show code and tests. Write a review checklist and explain one iteration you would make from feedback.
